claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi-derived high-entropy alloys exhibit high saturation magnetization.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi-derived high-entropy alloys have coercive fields below 100 Oe.
A heat treatment can induce controlled nanoscale secondary-phase precipitation within the fcc matrix.
Suitable isothermal aging or step-quenching conditions can favor secondary-phase nucleation and growth without degrading saturation magnetization.
The induced precipitates will be uniformly dispersed at the nanoscale within the fcc matrix.
The nanoscale precipitates may be ordered phases such as L1_2 or B2.
Nanoscale precipitates act as magnetic-domain-wall pinning centers.
Pinning by nanoscale precipitates increases the energy required for magnetic-domain reversal.
Increasing the energy required for domain reversal raises coercivity.
Controlled nanoscale precipitation will increase coercivity above 100 Oe relative to the original single-phase fcc alloy.
The precipitation treatment will retain high saturation magnetization.
Precipitate size and distribution determine whether the precipitates provide effective pinning without compromising saturation magnetization.
Direct evidence linking controlled nanoscale precipitation in fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys to improved coercivity is limited.
